details: TERRA-ANALOG is an interactive 3D web app that helps researchers and mission planners find places on Earth that resemble the surface of Mars and the Moon, where agencies test rovers, habitats and instruments before real missions. Users explore a photorealistic globe with a live day/night cycle, clouds and atmosphere. Red markers show Mars analogs (such as the Atacama Desert and Rio Tinto) and white markers show lunar analogs (such as Meteor Crater and Ries Crater). Clicking a site shows its similarity score, a five-axis radar chart, mineral and extremophile notes, and its testing history. A parameter matcher ranks the best Earth sites by temperature, aridity and soil type, and sites can be compared side by side. It makes analog research easier to explore and understand for planners, students and the public. We built it with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, globe.gl and three.js, and it runs in any modern browser. The creative part is combining a cinematic mission-control interface with a practical scientific matching tool. Site data is currently illustrative, and the next step is connecting real NASA and USGS datasets. The code was made by claude si made by Anthropic.
